title: RBAC accepted cookie-cached sessions after revocation
observedBehavior: The shared RBAC session lookup did not bypass Better Auth's five-minute cookie cache. The new revoked-session regression failed before the correction.
impact: A holder of an otherwise valid cached session could retain ordinary access after its backing session was revoked, until cache expiry. Fresh-auth paths had additional checks.
correction: Force disableCookieCache:true at the shared RBAC boundary. Current user, organization and permission checks still apply.
acceptance: Revoked authority returns no RBAC context before user lookup; active sessions still load current permissions; authority failure denies access.
confidence: high: source inspected; deployment not tested
rootCause: The shared RBAC session lookup did not bypass Better Auth's five-minute cookie cache. The new revoked-session regression failed before the correction.
alternativesAndTradeoffs: A shorter cookie cache reduces the revocation window but does not remove it. A live authority lookup closes that window at the cost of a session-store read on protected access.
changeRisk: low; adds a live session-store read and therefore latency/load
rollback: If session-store latency becomes unacceptable, optimize the live lookup or introduce verified invalidation; do not restore cached authority for revoked sessions.
milestoneUnlocked: Safer integration candidate; does not independently authorize pilot or production.
prerequisites: A previously issued valid cached session is presented after its backing record is revoked.
affectedAssets: Tenant data and ordinary authenticated operations.

title: Tenant photo uploads also have a public delivery path
observedBehavior: The upload action writes public/uploads/<organizationId>/ and returns /uploads/...; those static URLs bypass the guarded /api/uploads handler. The API separately advertised shared caching.
impact: Anyone with a static asset URL may access tenant photos where the host serves that public directory. No deployed exposure or access history was inspected.
correction: Implemented private, no-store for API responses. Remaining package P02 moves assets to private versioned storage, supplies authenticated delivery and closes the legacy public and optimized-image paths.
acceptance: API cache regression passes. Full closure additionally requires anonymous/foreign-tenant denial on both legacy and new URLs, authorized rendering/deletion, cache purge and migration hash reconciliation.
confidence: high: source inspected; deployment not tested
rootCause: The upload action writes public/uploads/<organizationId>/ and returns /uploads/...; those static URLs bypass the guarded /api/uploads handler. The API separately advertised shared caching.
alternativesAndTradeoffs: A private filesystem is simplest for one instance; private object storage supports multiple replicas and managed retention. Both require migration of stored references and image delivery.
dependencies: Private storage and legacy asset migration
effortEstimate: 3–5 engineering days including delivery consumers and migration verification; shared P02 estimate with F15
rollback: Keep copied originals private and switch to the previous authenticated delivery adapter on failure. Do not restore public URLs as a security rollback.
milestoneUnlocked: API cache defect corrected; public storage exposure remains a pilot/production blocker.
prerequisites: The deployment serves public/uploads and an unauthorized person obtains an asset URL.
affectedAssets: Uploaded tenant photos and related organization metadata.

title: Installed and CI Next.js versions precede the current security patch
observedBehavior: Installed/pnpm Next.js is 15.5.23; npm CI selects 15.5.18. The vendor August 25 release fixes two critical issues in 15.5.24. Local and CI dependency graphs also differ for React and Better Auth.
impact: The application can be built with a different and older security posture than the one tested locally. AVIF image optimization is an exposure candidate; the Windows issue additionally requires both routers. Exploitability and production topology are unverified.
correction: P01: update Next.js and its lint companion to the verified patched 15.5 line, reconcile the active lockfiles in an isolated install and bind CI evidence to that exact graph.
acceptance: Frozen installs resolve the intended patched version; dependency graph diff is reviewed; build, authentication, optimized images and key routes pass on the actual target OS.
confidence: confirmed version/advisory mismatch; conditional application exploitability
rootCause: Installed/pnpm Next.js is 15.5.23; npm CI selects 15.5.18. The vendor August 25 release fixes two critical issues in 15.5.24. Local and CI dependency graphs also differ for React and Better Auth.
alternativesAndTradeoffs: A patched maintenance release is a smaller compatibility change than a major framework upgrade. A temporary feature restriction can reduce exposure only after actual affected deployment paths are established.
dependencies: Reproducible isolated dependency install and build
effortEstimate: 1–2 days; separate from a framework major upgrade
rollback: Retain the previous lock graph for diagnosis. On incompatibility, withhold deployment or use a separately verified safe candidate; do not silently revert to an affected release.
milestoneUnlocked: Safer integration candidate; does not independently authorize pilot or production.
prerequisites: Affected framework or image-processing functionality must be reachable; the Windows route advisory additionally has vendor-specific router/configuration conditions. No exploit was reproduced.
affectedAssets: Application runtime, host process and data accessible to that process.

title: Spreadsheet import uses vulnerable SheetJS parser versions
observedBehavior: Both installed and npm-locked xlsx are 0.18.5. Browser import handlers read selected workbooks with XLSX.read. Vendor advisories cover prototype pollution through 0.19.2 and ReDoS through 0.20.1.
impact: A crafted workbook supplied to a user can affect the browser import workflow. Export-only call sites are not established as affected by the prototype-pollution advisory. No malicious workbook was executed.
correction: P01: use a verified official patched distribution (at least 0.20.2 for these advisories) or a maintained replacement. Pin its integrity; bound file/row sizes and isolate parsing from the main UI thread.
acceptance: Representative Excel files retain dates, decimals and headers; malformed and over-budget input is rejected; independently reviewed parser regression fixtures pass.
confidence: confirmed affected version and first-party parser use; deployed reachability not exercised
rootCause: Both installed and npm-locked xlsx are 0.18.5. Browser import handlers read selected workbooks with XLSX.read. Vendor advisories cover prototype pollution through 0.19.2 and ReDoS through 0.20.1.
alternativesAndTradeoffs: The official patched SheetJS distribution minimizes API changes; a replacement parser changes import behavior and needs compatibility fixtures. Worker isolation limits UI impact but does not replace the parser patch.
effortEstimate: 1–3 engineering days including focused verification; estimate, not a commitment
rollback: Temporarily disable affected spreadsheet import or retain the last verified safe parser; preserve uploaded inputs privately for retry.
milestoneUnlocked: Safer integration candidate; does not independently authorize pilot or production.
prerequisites: A user selects an adversarial workbook for the reachable browser import path.
affectedAssets: Import integrity, browser responsiveness and data processed in that session.

title: Finance query and export contracts prevented type checking
observedBehavior: Baseline type checking found four errors: Date[] filters supplied to string[] contracts, missing export audit watermark, and JSON omitted from the MIME mapping.
impact: Custom-date table state and export fingerprints were inconsistent with the shared query contract. JSON export completion and audit context were incomplete.
correction: Serialize valid dates once to ISO strings for both table and export queries, add the JSON MIME mapping and persist a tenant/request-bound watermark identifier in audit and job metadata.
acceptance: Repository type check passes; finance workbench tests and CSV/JSON worker-lease tests pass; export audit and durable job metadata contain the same watermark.
confidence: high: source inspected; deployment not tested
rootCause: Baseline type checking found four errors: Date[] filters supplied to string[] contracts, missing export audit watermark, and JSON omitted from the MIME mapping.
alternativesAndTradeoffs: A shared canonical filter map keeps table and export queries aligned. Type assertions would only hide the mismatch. A correlation identifier supports audit binding; physical watermark rendering remains a separate contract.
rollback: Revert only the changed filter/MIME/metadata logic if behavior regresses, retain queued export records and keep release blocked until the contract is repaired.
milestoneUnlocked: Safer integration candidate; does not independently authorize pilot or production.
limits: This binds an audit identifier. It does not establish that a configured renderer embeds it into every exported file; renderer/store/download/retention readiness remains separate.
prerequisites: A date-filtered finance query or declared JSON export is compiled/processed.
affectedAssets: Finance query consistency and export evidence.

title: API inventory reported ready with unclassified endpoints
observedBehavior: The previous inventory could report zero issues while six routes had unclassified guards and review-required module applicability. Every /api/auth/* route was broadly labeled public.
impact: A green static report could be interpreted as coverage of routes that the scanner had not understood.
correction: Unknown classification and module applicability now produce findings. The public Better Auth exception is limited to its exact catch-all route, and the authenticated permissions route is recognized.
acceptance: Unknown routes, including a new auth-prefix route, fail the gate; the protected claims route remains correctly classified; all 18 inventory tests pass.
confidence: high: source inspected; deployment not tested
rootCause: The previous inventory could report zero issues while six routes had unclassified guards and review-required module applicability. Every /api/auth/* route was broadly labeled public.
alternativesAndTradeoffs: Exact delegated-service mappings preserve public signed-link behavior while proving protection. Requiring ordinary sessions on every endpoint would break legitimate public links; broad directory exemptions hide new routes.
changeRisk: low code change; existing fail-mode gate now exposes six pending endpoint reviews
rollback: Keep unknown routes blocked. If a classification is incorrect, repair its exact mapping with a negative test instead of suppressing observations.
milestoneUnlocked: Safer integration candidate; does not independently authorize pilot or production.
limits: The current result is blocked with 12 observations across six routes. These are coverage gaps, not 12 demonstrated application vulnerabilities. Exact delegated-service mappings and negative tests are specified in P03.
prerequisites: A route lacks recognized guard/module classification, including new routes under the auth prefix.
affectedAssets: Release coverage claims and missed access-control review.

title: HTTPS session cookie was ignored by dashboard middleware
observedBehavior: The optimistic routing check recognized only better-auth.session_token, while Better Auth uses the __Secure- prefix for HTTPS.
impact: An otherwise signed-in HTTPS user could be redirected to login before reaching server authorization.
correction: Recognize both default cookie names. The shared server RBAC boundary still verifies the live session and permissions.
acceptance: Both supported cookie names reach server authorization; missing and unrelated cookies redirect to localized login with the original callback.
confidence: high: source inspected; deployment not tested
rootCause: The optimistic routing check recognized only better-auth.session_token, while Better Auth uses the __Secure- prefix for HTTPS.
alternativesAndTradeoffs: Recognizing the configured secure cookie preserves HTTPS behavior. Performing full session validation in middleware would duplicate the authoritative server check and add deployment coupling.
rollback: Preserve HTTPS recognition while correcting routing behavior; do not use cookie presence as permission or move authority away from the server.
milestoneUnlocked: Safer integration candidate; does not independently authorize pilot or production.
prerequisites: The authentication provider issues its default __Secure- session cookie over HTTPS.

title: Shared logger defaults to a silent sink
observedBehavior: lib/logger.ts initializes an empty sink. No first-party non-test caller of setLoggerSink was found in lib, services, app or actions; there is no root instrumentation entry point.
impact: Operational calls through this logger can disappear, undermining incident investigation. This does not mean database audit events or every other error logger are absent.
correction: P04: install a server startup sink using the existing canonical redaction rules, structured correlation IDs and an approved transport; add delivery health and failure behavior.
acceptance: A synthetic safe event from a protected operation reaches the configured sink and alert path; sensitive markers do not; transport failure is visible and does not corrupt a financial transaction.
confidence: confirmed default behavior and searched initialization gap; deployed injection/transport unknown
rootCause: lib/logger.ts initializes an empty sink. No first-party non-test caller of setLoggerSink was found in lib, services, app or actions; there is no root instrumentation entry point.
alternativesAndTradeoffs: A redacted structured stdout sink integrates with host collection; a dedicated transport provides explicit delivery control but adds failure handling. Choose based on the actual deployment.
dependencies: Approved log destination, retention and responsible operator
effortEstimate: 1–3 engineering days including focused verification; estimate, not a commitment
rollback: Route to a validated redacted fallback and flag transport failure; retain transactional database audit records independently.
milestoneUnlocked: Safer integration candidate; does not independently authorize pilot or production.
prerequisites: An operation emits through lib/logger without a registered sink. Other loggers and database audit records are separate.
affectedAssets: Operational detection, diagnosis and response evidence.

title: Middleware rate limit has process-local unbounded key retention
observedBehavior: Each new IP creates a Map entry; entries are not removed. The counter is per process and trusts forwarded IP headers without a verified proxy contract in this review.
impact: Long-lived instances can accumulate keys, while multiple instances do not share a limit. Spoofing depends on ingress header sanitization, which was not tested.
correction: P04: define trusted ingress identity, use a bounded local fallback with expiry and a shared limiter for sensitive operations; measure behavior across replicas.
acceptance: Expired keys are reclaimed; configured limits hold across two workers; spoofed client-supplied headers cannot evade the trusted ingress limit.
confidence: confirmed local structure; ingress bypass is an untested deployment hypothesis
rootCause: Each new IP creates a Map entry; entries are not removed. The counter is per process and trusts forwarded IP headers without a verified proxy contract in this review.
alternativesAndTradeoffs: An expiring bounded Map limits single-process memory; a shared limiter enforces cross-replica quotas but requires a reliable store and a clear failure policy. Ingress header trust must be explicit.
effortEstimate: 1–3 engineering days including focused verification; estimate, not a commitment
rollback: Use a bounded conservative local fallback during shared-store failure and alert the operator; retain trusted-ingress validation.
milestoneUnlocked: Safer integration candidate; does not independently authorize pilot or production.
prerequisites: Numerous distinct keys reach the process; cross-replica evasion or forwarded-header spoofing depends on deployment topology.
affectedAssets: Runtime memory, fair-use limits and service availability.

title: Historical analytics COGS depends on current item cost
observedBehavior: Financial analytics computes historical COGS as sale-line quantity multiplied by the related item's current costPrice. SalesOrderLine has no immutable cost snapshot in the inspected schema.
impact: Editing an item's cost can change reported historical margins without a new accounting event. This is an analytical read-model issue; this review does not establish ledger corruption.
correction: P05: derive recognized COGS from the existing posted inventory valuation/ledger source for that sale and period. Show unavailable/unreconciled status when historical provenance is missing instead of inferring current cost.
acceptance: Change an item's current cost after a posted sale; prior-period recognized COGS remains unchanged and reconciles to ledger/valuation evidence, including returns and partial deliveries.
confidence: high: source inspected; deployment not tested
rootCause: Financial analytics computes historical COGS as sale-line quantity multiplied by the related item's current costPrice. SalesOrderLine has no immutable cost snapshot in the inspected schema.
alternativesAndTradeoffs: Posted valuation provides historical recognition truth. Snapshotting current cost could prevent future changes but cannot reconstruct missing historical cost or reliably handle returns.
dependencies: Finance owner confirms recognized-cost and recognition-date semantics
changeRisk: high for historical metric meaning; stage read-model replacement, do not rewrite journal history
rollback: Keep the old calculation available only as a clearly labeled estimate while the new read model is disabled; never rewrite posted journals or claim estimates reconcile.
milestoneUnlocked: Safer integration candidate; does not independently authorize pilot or production.
prerequisites: An item cost changes after a sale and historical analytics are recalculated.
affectedAssets: Historical margin, recognized COGS and operational decisions.

confidence: high: source inspected; deployment not tested

title: Native approval register remains a blueprint
observedBehavior: The proposed native register models and approval route are absent. The provider contract and local simulator do not establish an operating native approval authority.
impact: Users cannot yet obtain native issued approval IDs, verification references or durable signed-record links from that proposal.
correction: P07 implements the blueprint in stages: verified owner establishment, scoped appointments, immutable request revisions/private artifacts, authenticated decisions, validity checks, then Copy X1 fields.
acceptance: No prior register ID is required to start establishment; real authority and verification are required to activate it. Cross-tenant, self-approval, stale revision, replay, expiry and revocation tests pass; human decisions remain distinct from POL-004 automation.
confidence: high: source inspected; deployment not tested
rootCause: The proposed native register models and approval route are absent. The provider contract and local simulator do not establish an operating native approval authority.
alternativesAndTradeoffs: A native register gives consistent tenant scope and automatic references; an existing recognized external register reduces implementation scope. First-time establishment needs real authority evidence, not an earlier system ID.
dependencies: Owner authority evidence, establishment verifier, role appointments, signing/retention decisions
effortEstimate: multi-stage package; estimate after storage and identity choices
rollback: Disable new decision issuance and preserve immutable signed records/events. A corrected version can supersede eligibility without deleting history.
milestoneUnlocked: Safer integration candidate; does not independently authorize pilot or production.
limits: No native register, signature or approval was created by this audit.
prerequisites: Users need issued approval references while only blueprint documents/provider contracts exist.
affectedAssets: Approval authority, signature evidence and gate eligibility.

title: Reversal numbers use count-plus-one allocation
observedBehavior: Reversal entry numbers are allocated by counting existing daily entries inside a default-isolation transaction. A tenant/entry-number unique constraint exists.
impact: Concurrent reversals of different entries can select the same number and cause one transaction to fail. The unique constraint prevents this alone from proving duplicate entry numbers or double posting.
correction: P05: reproduce with two real PostgreSQL transactions, then use a scoped sequence/counter or bounded conflict retry that preserves posting idempotency.
acceptance: Concurrent independent reversals both complete with distinct numbers, or return an explicit retryable conflict with no partial journal, event or close-invalidation writes.
confidence: source-supported race candidate; not reproduced against PostgreSQL
rootCause: Reversal entry numbers are allocated by counting existing daily entries inside a default-isolation transaction. A tenant/entry-number unique constraint exists.
alternativesAndTradeoffs: A scoped sequence allocates reliably but needs a database design; bounded conflict retry is smaller but must rerun the whole transaction and preserve idempotency. Reproduce the actual collision first.
effortEstimate: 1–3 engineering days including focused verification; estimate, not a commitment
rollback: Stop the new allocator, retain all assigned numbers and use a verified transactional fallback. Never renumber or delete posted entries.
milestoneUnlocked: Safer integration candidate; does not independently authorize pilot or production.
prerequisites: Two independent reversals allocate the same tenant/date number concurrently; the unique constraint prevents duplicate persisted numbers, so the suspected failure is an aborted request.
affectedAssets: Journal availability and atomic reversal/close-invalidation behavior.

title: Timeout rejects the caller without cancelling the operation
observedBehavior: withAgentExecutionTimeout races a timer against an operation and clears only the timer. Its contract carries no AbortSignal or deadline to the underlying operation.
impact: A timed-out read can continue consuming resources. Current registered tools are constrained to read-only; this is not evidence of unauthorized financial writes.
correction: P04: pass deadlines/cancellation to adapters that support them and fence any late persistence using run/lease state. Bound uncancellable reads independently.
acceptance: A deliberately slow adapter is cancelled or bounded, late completion cannot change a terminal run, and timeout metrics agree with observed in-flight work.
confidence: confirmed promise semantics; full adapter cancellation behavior not tested
rootCause: withAgentExecutionTimeout races a timer against an operation and clears only the timer. Its contract carries no AbortSignal or deadline to the underlying operation.
alternativesAndTradeoffs: Cancellation frees resources when supported; deadline-limited reads and lease fences bound uncancellable work. Racing a timer alone changes the caller response but cannot stop an adapter.
dependencies: Adapter cancellation and database timeout contracts
effortEstimate: 1–3 engineering days including focused verification; estimate, not a commitment
rollback: Disable affected tools or enforce conservative deadlines while repairing cancellation; keep the terminal-state fence and attempt history.
milestoneUnlocked: Safer integration candidate; does not independently authorize pilot or production.
prerequisites: A tool adapter continues beyond its caller timeout. Inspected registered tools are read-only.
affectedAssets: Compute/provider budget and truthful run status.

title: Storage configuration updates are not durable
observedBehavior: The read path builds defaults and the update path returns a constructed configuration without a durable persistence write in the inspected implementation.
impact: A settings change can appear successful and be lost on the next read; local/online selection and limits can diverge from the UI.
correction: Include durable tenant-scoped configuration and revision checks in P02, with server-side validation and the existing fresh-auth permission boundary.
acceptance: Change storage mode and size limit, then read through a new request/process and observe the same authorized revision; denied users cannot change it.
confidence: high: source inspected; deployment not tested
rootCause: The read path builds defaults and the update path returns a constructed configuration without a durable persistence write in the inspected implementation.
alternativesAndTradeoffs: A tenant configuration model supports durable scoped settings. Environment-only settings are simpler but should be read-only in the UI rather than pretending to save tenant changes.
dependencies: Storage backend configuration model and migration
effortEstimate: 1–3 engineering days including focused verification; estimate, not a commitment
rollback: Retain configuration revisions, stop new writes and restore the last valid private backend revision; do not switch existing private assets to public delivery.
milestoneUnlocked: Safer integration candidate; does not independently authorize pilot or production.
prerequisites: A user saves storage settings and a later request re-reads defaults.
affectedAssets: Storage control expectations, upload limits and configuration consistency.

title: Database diagnostic printed credential-bearing URLs
observedBehavior: The local diagnostic interpolated the full database connection URL into success and failure logs; the failure also exposed the raw error message.
impact: Running it with a credential-bearing URL could disclose credentials to terminal/log history. This audit did not run the diagnostic or establish a past leak.
correction: Replace those messages with fixed success/failure text; do not output URL or raw driver errors.
acceptance: Static inspection confirms both messages omit URL and driver error interpolation. Runtime diagnostic deliberately not executed.
confidence: high: source inspected; deployment not tested
rootCause: The local diagnostic interpolated the full database connection URL into success and failure logs; the failure also exposed the raw error message.
alternativesAndTradeoffs: Fixed messages avoid credential leakage; a reviewed allowlisted diagnostic can expose safe error codes if troubleshooting needs more detail. Raw URLs or driver messages should not return.
rollback: Do not restore credential logging; add a reviewed masked diagnostic formatter if detail is needed.
milestoneUnlocked: Safer integration candidate; does not independently authorize pilot or production.
prerequisites: Someone runs the local diagnostic with a credential-bearing connection URL and its output is retained or shared. No actual leaked value/history was inspected.
affectedAssets: Database credentials and access to the referenced database.

title: Finance presentation and responsive test contracts were out of sync
observedBehavior: A final drift-triggered recheck reproduced four failures: financial-statement controls and cash-flow pagination lacked shared presentation markers; the selection test assumed only one responsive checkbox; a global date-picker count rejected an additional valid picker.
impact: Shared table spacing/control rules were not applied consistently, and stale tests blocked verification of legitimate responsive changes.
rootCause: New and adapted table surfaces did not retain all shared classes; two tests coupled their expectations to old markup counts instead of current behavior.
correction: Restore the existing shared toolbar/pagination classes. Scope the desktop selection action to its table, verify both desktop/mobile controls share state in both directions, and require the shared date picker separately in every named query surface.
alternativesAndTradeoffs: Adding broad test exclusions or increasing the aggregate count would obscure individual missing integrations. Per-surface checks and cross-layout selection verify the intended contract while allowing additional responsive markup.
confidence: High: four failures reproduced on an unchanged source snapshot; focused verification after correction is retained.
prerequisites: The current working tree includes the newer responsive table implementations.
affectedAssets: Finance presentation consistency and reliable local verification.
changeRisk: Low: three existing CSS class bindings and focused test corrections; browser appearance still needs X1 proof.
acceptance: All eight affected suites pass; every query surface uses the shared picker; desktop/mobile selection stays synchronized; table presentation scans detect no missing toolbar or pagination markers.
rollback: Revert only the added class tokens if a verified visual regression occurs and repair the shared style contract. Preserve the behavior-based tests; do not reinstate arbitrary global counts.
milestoneUnlocked: Reliable local finance verification; does not establish authenticated X1 capture or performance acceptance.
limits: The finance dashboard was also changed by another concurrent workstream. Only the added pagination class is attributed to this audit. JSDOM does not establish viewport CSS or screen-reader behavior.
